# Callsign Listening Practice

`Training → RX Callsigns` plays one generated callsign, waits for you to key it back, then scores each character in its proper position. It draws from the [callsign generator](501-callsign-generator.md), so familiar prefixes return without the rest of the call becoming a rehearsed answer.

Under `Settings → RX Callsigns`, `4-6`, `4-5`, and `5-6` choose a fresh length at random within the named range for each call; `4`, `5`, and `6` keep it fixed. That is all the notation is trying to say.

Use a fixed length for steady difficulty, then a range when you catch yourself guessing where the callsign ends. Calls on air do not arrive with the character count printed on the front, which is inconsiderate but traditional.

For the same callsigns without having to key an answer, use [Passive Listening](250-passive-listening.md).
